cohort: 1,511 women served by nursing student birth doulas (Birth Companions) between 1998 and 2014
finding: Vulnerable mothers (refugees, non-English speakers, teens, low income, low education) who received support from Birth Companions had higher rates of epidural use and smaller babies, and were less likely to attempt breastfeeding, but there was no difference in other birth outcomes.
mod_finding: There was no difference in the frequency of caesarean births between vulnerable and non-vulnerable women.
birth_weight: Smaller babies born to vulnerable mothers
